feed.title: Brad Lasater — Research Log
feed.subtitle: Building a systematic volatility trading system in the open: what I tried, what I expected, what happened, and what I had wrong.

entry.title: Every price in this system is a traded price, and that changes which tests are even meaningful
entry.summary: Option NBBO is a 403 on this data tier, so implied volatility is inverted from last trade or day close rather than from a quote midpoint. The consequence is not merely noisier numbers — it invalidates one of the three daily identity checks whenever either leg of a pair is a stale print, and it makes the spread-based cost model uncalibratable rather than approximate.

entry.title: Half my datasets can be backfilled and half cannot, and that decides what a replay may claim
entry.summary: Option day bars reach back to 2022-08-31 and can be rebuilt from the vendor archive at any time; chain snapshots exist only from 2026-08-31 because there is no historical snapshot endpoint. That asymmetry, not storage cost, is what limits which backtests this system will ever be allowed to run.

entry.title: The ATM term structure agrees with itself by construction, so I had to work out when its agreement is evidence
entry.summary: The term structure inverts both the call and the put at the at-the-money strike and writes out both. When put-call parity happens to select that same strike, the two legs invert to identical volatilities as an algebraic identity — so their agreement proves nothing, and only the dates where the two strikes differ carry information.
